newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK commercial property market seen firmer in 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK commercial property market seen firmer in 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong's commercial property market is expected to improve in 1997 with strengthening demand to offset oversupply in both the office and retail sectors, property consultancy Brooke Hillier Parker said on Tuesday.
The consultancy forecast a rise of between five and 10 percent in rents and sales prices in both the office and retail markets this year, said partner David Faulker.
This compared with a 13 percent fall in rents and a five percent rise in prices of offices last year, and a five and six percent gain respectively in rents and prices in the retail sector in 1996.
Most of office rent fall in 1996 came in the first half of the year due to the economic slowdown in Hong Kong and China, the consultancy said.
It said take-up of prime office space increased in the second half of the year following an improved economic outlook in China and Hong Kong later in the year.
Demand for offices was expected to rise to balance out an anticipated growth in supply in 1998 and 1999, it added.
Hong Kong is still the most expensive office location in the region, with average prime rents of HK$66 per square foot per month against Tokyo's HK$64 a sq ft, Brooke Hillier Parker said.

But Hong Kong is now more competitive cost-wise than before and many companies that were considering relocation from Hong Kong to save on costs are rethinking their plans with most choosing to stay in the territory, it added.
